findings.summary: FinCEN issued a consent order assessing a $1.3 billion civil money penalty against TD Bank for BSA/AML violations, crediting $543 million toward DOJ and OCC payments, leaving a net $757 million payable to the Treasury.
The OCC issued a cease and desist order, imposed a $450 million civil money penalty, and placed growth restrictions on TD Bank for BSA/AML deficiencies.
The CFPB ordered TD Bank to pay $7.76 million in redress to consumers and a $20 million civil money penalty ($28 million total) for furnishing inaccurate credit information.
OFAC settled with TD Bank for $115,005.04 to resolve apparent violations of North Korea sanctions and foreign narcotics kingpin sanctions.
The CFTC ordered TD Bank to pay a $75 million civil monetary penalty for recordkeeping and supervision failures related to unapproved communication methods.
TD Bank N.A. and its parent TD Bank US Holding Company pleaded guilty to conspiracy to launder money, agreeing to pay a combined $1.8 billion in penalties and to remediate its AML program.
TD Bank paid $32,225,000 in 2025 to settle the Burns APSN overdraft fees class action, denying wrongdoing.
Trisal v. TD Bank was filed on October 2, 2025 alleging TD Bank failed to refund overdraft fees per its grace‑period policy.
Federal court records show the Trisal grace‑period suit against TD Bank was terminated on May 15, 2026.
The Ontario Superior Court approved a settlement on February 15, 2024 for the TD Bank duplicative NSF fees class action covering fees charged from February 2, 2019 to November 27, 2023.

On October 10, 2024 TD Bank pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit money laundering and agreed to pay $1.8 billion, while US regulators imposed $3.09 billion in monetary penalties and business restrictions.

The Rochon Genova class action alleging misrepresentations about TD Bank’s AML controls filed an amended claim on November 4, 2024 and was concluded on July 23 2026 after certification hearings in February 2026.
On October 13, 2026 a U.S. District Court denied in part TD Bank’s motion to dismiss, allowing a securities fraud lawsuit alleging AML misstatements to proceed.
The Ontario Superior Court certified on April 10, 2026 a class action claiming TD Bank failed to pay vacation and holiday pay to commissioned mobile mortgage specialists.
On November 26, 2025 a New Jersey federal court dismissed a securities class action against TD Bank finding plaintiffs lacked standing as non‑purchasers/sellers of TD securities.
A class action lawsuit was filed on October 22, 2024 alleging TD Bank made false and misleading statements about its AML program during the class period.

TD Bank N.A. and its parent TD Bank US Holding Company pleaded guilty to conspiring to fail to maintain an AML program, fail to file accurate Currency Transaction Reports, and launder money, agreeing to pay approximately $1.8 billion in penalties (reported as up to $3 billion) and to remediate their AML compliance program.

Former TD Bank assistant store manager Wilfredo Aquino pleaded guilty to conspiring to launder monetary instruments, having facilitated the movement of approximately $474 million through TD Bank accounts for a money‑laundering network.
Wilfredo Aquino was sentenced to prison for facilitating money laundering, having previously pleaded guilty to conspiring to launder monetary instruments.

TD Bank employee Nunez pleaded guilty to facilitating a Colombian ATM money‑laundering scheme, moving over $26 million from the United States to Colombia via hundreds of debit cards and ATM withdrawals.
Former TD Bank employee Leonardo Ayala pleaded guilty to conspiring to launder monetary instruments and receiving bribes, having laundered approximately $5.5 million to Colombia.
Leonardo Ayala was sentenced to two years in prison and three years of supervised release for accepting bribes and laundering more than $5.5 million to Colombia.

Former TD Bank employee Wilfredo Aquino pleaded guilty to conspiring to launder monetary instruments and receiving bribes, having laundered approximately $4.8 million to Colombia and received over $8,000 in bribes.

OFAC settled with TD Bank, N.A. for $115,005.04 over apparent violations of the North Korea Sanctions Regulations and the Foreign Narcotics Kingpin Sanctions Regulations, including processing transactions for North Korean UN mission employees and maintaining accounts for a specially designated national.

Between December 22, 2025 and March 11, 2026, a TD Bank employee accessed and misused customer account information, prompting a May 2026 data breach lawsuit investigation; notifications to affected customers began around May 26, 2026.
In January 2026, an insider threat compromised TD Bank customers' personal data including names, Social Security numbers, and account details; the breach was confirmed and reported on June 15, 2026.

On August 27, 2026, a TD Bank employee compromised personal information of two New Hampshire customers, including names, addresses, Social Security numbers and account numbers; the bank notified affected parties and offered two years of free credit monitoring.
On May 15, 2026, TD Bank U.S. reported a data breach affecting two Massachusetts residents, exposing Social Security numbers and financial account information.
On September 4, 2026, TD Bank reported a data breach affecting 54 Massachusetts residents, exposing financial account information (but not Social Security numbers).
On November 20, 2026, TD Bank reported a data breach affecting two Massachusetts residents, exposing Social Security numbers only.
CFPB ordered TD Bank to pay $28 million for illegally furnishing inaccurate consumer credit report data, citing management prioritizing growth over compliance.
TD Bank faced a $3 billion fine for compliance failures after ignoring internal whistleblower warnings, with whistleblowers reporting concerns internally before turning to regulators.

Following AML failures, TD Bank reduced CEO Masrani's 2024 compensation to $1.5 million (down 89%) and cut variable pay for 41 executives by a total of $30 million, reflecting executive accountability for governance shortcomings.
